newsitem.title: USA: EXCEL says switching complaints unwarranted.
newsitem.headline: EXCEL says switching complaints unwarranted.

text.p: EXCEL Communications Inc said Friday it plans to appeal a decision by the Better Business Bureau of Metropolitan Dallas to revoke its membership.
The company said it plans to meet Monday, September 23 with the bureau's president, Ronald Berry, to discuss the matter. It said it is confident it can resolve the matter at the meeting.
The Better Business Bureau received complaints about alleged unauthorized switching by EXCEL, which provides residential, long-distance telecommunications service.
EXCEL said it responded to an inquiry by the bureau in August based on customer complaints, and believed it had resolved the issue.
EXCEL said it did not receive further contact from the Better Business Bureau until Thursday, when the company called in response to an inquriy by the media.

"We were shocked and absolutely disagree with the BBB's decision," company President and Chief Executive Kenny Troutt said in a statement. "EXCEL has an exemplary track record in strictly prohibiting and actively reducing all violations of company policy, including unauthorized switching."
EXCEL has been a member of the Better Business Bureau of Metropolitan Dallas since 1990.
